Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Card or optical module hardware fault".

state: [2026-11-22 Handover Note · Night Shift to Day Shift] Around 08:43, the DEV-0331 base station at S-471 went out of service. On the network management side, the RRU link was seen as disconnected, and the cell out-of-service alarm lasted 27 minutes. Voice and data services for about 340 subscribers under it were completely cut off. A phone call has been made to the on-site duty staff, who replied that the base station yard gate can be opened and the mains power is normal, but the feeder cable on the tower and the optical cable joint box are both inside the yard, requiring tower climbing and box opening for inspection. It cannot be determined remotely whether the issue is the optical module or water ingress in the feeder cable, so personnel must be dispatched to the site to handle it; this is not within the scope of remote resolution. According to the grading criteria: affecting 300 or more subscribers and the out-of-service condition not yet restored counts as 60 points; out of service for more than 15 minutes adds 20 points, for a cumulative 80 points; 80 points or more is directly classified as emergency. The equipment belongs to the access section and the antenna feeder external line, and is the responsibility of the on-site operations and maintenance desk; there are no related alarms for this station on the transmission and core network sides. In addition, during the day shift, please hand the spare parts receipt for TK-20261028-8752 to the warehouse; don't forget. Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Field operations, access segment and outside plant".

Please return the matter within today. Note: The contract with the seal of SO-20261026-832335 should be followed up by the administration side; it is unrelated to this document. Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Core team, routing and backbone equipment".

state: [Meeting Minutes Excerpt · Capacity Review] Topic: Reconsideration of the CS-005475(S-845 DEV-2046) expansion application. Data reference: Peak utilization rate during busy hours is 91.2% (based on the maximum sampling value of the past 7 days). Gear mapping: Below 50% is Tier 0, 50% to 70% is Tier 1, 70% to 85% is Tier 2, 85% to 95% is Tier 3, and 95% or above is Tier 4. Therefore, this article falls under Tier 3. Expansion determination: Tier 2 and above are considered to require capacity expansion; Tiers 0 and 1 are considered not needed temporarily. Action determination sequence: first look at level 4—directly expand the existing link; Next, look at level 3—if the peak in neighboring areas is less than 60% during busy times, prioritize diversion; if all neighbors are not below 60%, expand the existing link; Continue observation when there is no shunt margin at the second gear; Level 1 observation; Gear 0 remains the status quo. The peak peak times for the two neighboring districts in this object are 87% and 89%, respectively, both not below 60%, with no room for diversion. Therefore, the existing link is being expanded and included in next month's batch. Note: C-93221 The voice quality issue complained about last week was handled separately by the wireless optimization team and is unrelated to this topic. Supplementary conclusion: this case does not amount to "Add capacity to the existing link or cell".
